draft.title: Convection
card: A fluid is a liquid or a gas. Its particles can move from place to place, so they can carry heat with them.
When part of a fluid is heated, its particles spread out. The warm fluid becomes less dense than the fluid around it, so it rises.
Cooler fluid is more dense, so it sinks to take the place of the rising fluid.
This loop of rising warm fluid and sinking cool fluid is a convection current. It happens in liquids and gases, but not in solids.
draft.remember: Warm fluid rises and cool fluid sinks, making a convection current that carries heat.

a.q: Why does warm water rise in a pot heated from below?
opts: It is less dense than the cooler water around it
It is more dense than the cooler water around it
Its particles shrink and become lighter
Its particles pass heat on by collisions only
a.why: Heated water spreads out, so the same amount takes up more space and is less dense. It floats upward through the cooler water. It does not become more dense, which would make it sink.
a.clue: Think about what spreading out does to density.

b.q: Sam's classroom in Darwin has a heater on the floor. What happens to the air in the room?
opts: Warm air rises and cooler air sinks, forming a current
Warm air sinks and cooler air rises, forming a current
Warm air stays by the heater and nothing else moves
Heat passes along the air only by particle collisions
b.why: Air by the heater warms, spreads out and rises, and cooler air sinks to replace it. This makes a convection current. The reverse order is wrong because warm air is less dense, not more.
b.clue: Which air is less dense, warm or cool?

a.best: It is less dense than the cooler water around it

b.best: Warm air rises and cooler air sinks, forming a current

problems.detail: Setting the floor heater in a Darwin classroom is implausible, as Darwin is tropical and hot all year. It may distract or confuse students; a cooler city such as Hobart or Canberra would fit better.

check.summary: The science on the card, questions and explanations is correct, and the intended answers match. The only issue is that question b sets a classroom heater in tropical Darwin, which is an odd and possibly distracting choice.
